summary: Chelan County L-4 cab built 1933 on Wenatchee National Forest; gone by 1973, and the summit is open to a scramble from Nason Ridge Trail.

access.note: On Wenatchee National Forest land; the Forest Service describes a scramble to the summit from Nason Ridge Trail

visit.trail_note: Scramble to the summit from the west end of Nason Ridge Trail, where it meets the Snowy Creek trail

facts.status_note: Cab removed in 1973 (one source says destroyed); the Forest Service says the lookout is no longer there

events.note: Jim Coston named as the Rock Mountain lookout in June 1933
Haven Bachelor named as lookout in June 1934; Mrs. Bachelor expected to spend most of the summer there
Register says removed; firelookout.com says destroyed
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on October 28, 2012

evidence.quote: This L-4 cab, built in 1933, was removed in 1973.
This L-4 cab, built in 1933, was destroyed in 1973.

evidence.supports: about 7 miles northeast of Stevens Pass
Jim Coston item attributed to The Leavenworth Echo
Haven Bachelor lookout June 1934; Mrs. Bachelor expected to spend the summer there
evidence.quote: Haven Bachelor is lookout on Rock mountain and Mrs. Bachelor expects to spend most of the summer with him there.

evidence.supports: Haven Bachelor item attributed to The Wenatchee Daily World
lookout no longer there; summit gives views
evidence.quote: The lookout is no longer there, but the summit provides great views of the cascade range.

evidence.supports: scramble to summit from trail junction
evidence.quote: On the west end of the ridge where the trail meets the Snowy Creek trail, you can scramble to the summit of Rock Mountain, which is the site of an old fire lookout.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the cab was removed in 1973; firelookout.com says it was destroyed that year. Both agree it was gone by 1973.

sources.title: Rock Mountain Lookout Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites Register, Forest Fire Lookout Association

sources.title: Trail - Nason Ridge Trail
sources.publisher: USDA Forest Service, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest

notes_for_editor: Dates for the 1933 build and 1973 end agree across sources, but the register says removed and firelookout.com says destroyed. The 1933 and 1934 staffing items come from a visitor site's transcriptions of newspaper items; the newspapers themselves were not checked. No usable photo found and the 1934 panoramas were not located. The scramble access is the Forest Service's description and was not verified on the ground. Story is short because the sources are thin.
